candidate.title: CLIP / HITS-CLIP
candidate.scope: Grouped CLIP / HITS-CLIP architecture of the assigned Illumina poster row: a protein-associated RNA substrate is UV-crosslinked at 254 nm, RNase T1-trimmed, proteinase K-treated, extracted and copied into cDNA. The left expansion reads "Crosslinking and immunoprecipitation sequencing (CLIP) or high-throughput sequencing of CLIP cDNA library (HITS-CLIP)"; its icon is descriptive, not a second branch. CLIP is the crosslinking/immunoprecipitation assay, and HITS-CLIP adds high-throughput sequencing of recovered CLIP material. The graph records the five displayed transformation blocks and their material interfaces, ending at cDNA; sequencing is downstream context, not an extra drawn operation. Target-protein immunoprecipitation is essential to interpreting the named assays but is not drawn in this row; primary-supported selection is explained without inventing its position relative to RNase T1. The shared T1 schematic is not a claim that all complete CLIP and HITS-CLIP protocols use the same nuclease or preparation. Adjacent Ribo-Seq/GTI-Seq/ARTseq, RIP-Seq, Pol II CLIP and partial uridine/pseudouridine structures are excluded. Other methods and adaptations mentioned only in the catalogue or papers do not add target workflows.
